title: Extensible charts for SPFx Adaptive Card Extensions.
summary: Viva Connections data visualization across web and mobile.
problem: Developers needed a straightforward way to configure useful charts in Adaptive Card Extensions (ACEs), with extensible APIs and consistent behavior across web and mobile.
contribution: I owned API and type-contract design, shared label-generation logic across web and mobile, and web rendering for line and multiline charts. I then owned bar-chart APIs and rendering across both platforms. The broader feature was collaborative: I worked with other engineers and design partners on layouts, data scenarios, localization, RTL, accessibility, and theme behavior, and supported testing, developer guidance, and technical demos.
outcome: Delivered developer-facing charting capabilities and integration guidance. I also co-presented the public feature demo on Microsoft Community Learning.
judgment: Reuse is valuable when it preserves a coherent experience—not simply when it reduces the amount of code.

title: Analytics across 3 organizations and 17 teams.
summary: End-to-end ownership of a new service and partner integration.
problem: Product analytics needed more complete coverage across usage surfaces and partner-owned systems.
contribution: I owned the effort from design through implementation and staged validation. I created a new C#/.NET service and repository from scratch, implemented event-driven ingestion with Azure Event Hubs and Azure Cosmos DB, and coordinated integration across 3 organizations and 17 teams.
outcome: New service and partner integration built, with staged validation. Production rollout is not confirmed.
judgment: The central challenge was aligning dependencies and validation across teams while maintaining a single accountable owner for the integration.

title: Finding the simpler path to a shipped feature.
summary: Pragmatic product design and cross-team delivery.
problem: A content-sharing feature began with a more complex integration approach than the user task required.
contribution: I investigated the options, helped identify a simpler approach, aligned it with the product's interaction model, refined the interface, and coordinated delivery with partner teams.
outcome: Contributed to delivery through general availability while removing an unnecessary integration dependency.
judgment: The useful design question is often what does not need to be built. Simplifying the path should preserve the scope users actually need.

title: Turning measurements into dependable experiences.
summary: Mobile reliability, accessible interaction, and partner ownership.
problem: User-visible failures crossed code-ownership boundaries, and the measurements themselves needed validation.
contribution: I investigated failures, built monitoring views, coordinated fixes with partner engineers, and guided a small reliability workstream. Alongside that work, I delivered loading and recovery interactions and addressed accessibility gaps.
outcome: Contributed shipped mobile-quality improvements and monitoring that supported ongoing reliability work.
judgment: Reproducible user scenarios make disagreement constructive. Test delayed content, recovery, and different input methods—not just the normal path.
